findings.body: The UI advertises an extra page and permits navigating to it; that page requests an offset equal to the total and renders an empty member list.
findings.failure_mode: Pagination exposes a non-existent page with no members.
findings.impact: The UI advertises an extra page and permits navigating to it; that page requests an offset equal to the total and renders an empty member list.
findings.root_cause: The total-page calculation uses floor division and then unconditionally adds one.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (while retaining the zero-member special case) so an exact final page does not create a phantom next page.
findings.title: Compute the page count with ceiling division
findings.trigger: An admin views a group whose membership count is an exact multiple of the page limit, such as 50 or 100 members with the default limit of 50.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 exists verbatim with `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 users with limit 50), floor(50/50)+1=2 pages, but only 1 page of data exists. The patch introduces this calculation, creating a phantom empty final page.

findings.body: The automatic-group protection test still passes because it invokes the action as PUT, even though the newly added production endpoint is DELETE, leaving the actual removal request path unverified.
findings.failure_mode: The test suite does not cover the HTTP method used by production member removals.
findings.impact: The automatic-group protection test still passes because it invokes the action as PUT, even though the newly added production endpoint is DELETE, leaving the actual removal request path unverified.
findings.root_cause: The new test uses PUT despite the added member-removal route and client request both using DELETE.
findings.suggested_fix: Change this example to `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` and, if applicable, add a request/routing assertion for `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`.
findings.title: Exercise automatic-member removal with the routed HTTP verb
findings.trigger: The DELETE members route or DELETE-specific request handling regresses while the controller action itself remains callable in controller specs.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 115 shows `xhr :put, :remove_member` while line 125 shows the success case uses `xhr :delete, :remove_member`. The routes.rb shows `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. The automatic-group protection test uses PUT but production uses DELETE, leaving the DELETE path untested for automatic groups.

raw_findings.body: The UI advertises an extra page and permits navigating to it; that page requests an offset equal to the total and renders an empty member list.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Pagination exposes a non-existent page with no members.
raw_findings.impact: The UI advertises an extra page and permits navigating to it; that page requests an offset equal to the total and renders an empty member list.
raw_findings.root_cause: The total-page calculation uses floor division and then unconditionally adds one.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (while retaining the zero-member special case) so an exact final page does not create a phantom next page.
raw_findings.title: Compute the page count with ceiling division
raw_findings.trigger: An admin views a group whose membership count is an exact multiple of the page limit, such as 50 or 100 members with the default limit of 50.

raw_findings.body: Each item view is scoped to a member, which has no `automatic` property, so the condition is false and the UI displays remove buttons for a group whose membership cannot be changed. Clicking one reaches the server-side automatic-group rejection rather than removing the member.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The administrative UI offers an operation that is guaranteed to fail for automatic groups.
raw_findings.impact: Each item view is scoped to a member, which has no `automatic` property, so the condition is false and the UI displays remove buttons for a group whose membership cannot be changed. Clicking one reaches the server-side automatic-group rejection rather than removing the member.
raw_findings.root_cause: The template checks an unqualified `automatic` value in the per-member item-view context instead of the containing group.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the parent group's automatic state into the item view or reference the parent controller/group explicitly when deciding whether to render the remove link.
raw_findings.title: Do not render removal controls for automatic groups
raw_findings.trigger: An admin opens an automatic group with members.

raw_findings.body: The endpoint returns an empty page with offset 50 even though members still exist on page one; the admin remains on an empty member list until manually navigating back.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A valid group member list is rendered empty after deleting the last member on a partial final page.
raw_findings.impact: The endpoint returns an empty page with offset 50 even though members still exist on page one; the admin remains on an empty member list until manually navigating back.
raw_findings.root_cause: The endpoint calculates the current total but applies the requested offset unchanged, including offsets that became invalid due to a concurrent membership deletion.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After calculating `total`, clamp the requested offset to the highest valid page start (and return that normalized offset), or have the client detect and refetch an out-of-range final page.
raw_findings.title: Normalize offsets after the member total shrinks
raw_findings.trigger: An admin is on the final partial page of a group (for example offset 50 of 51 members) and removes its only member, causing the client reload to request offset 50 after the total has become 50.

raw_findings.body: The controller no longer reads `params[:group][:name]`, so it attempts to save an empty-name group and returns validation failure instead of creating the requested group.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Previously functioning clients cannot create groups after the server update.
raw_findings.impact: The controller no longer reads `params[:group][:name]`, so it attempts to save an empty-name group and returns validation failure instead of creating the requested group.
raw_findings.root_cause: Create input parsing was changed from the established `params[:group]` object to only top-level parameters.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept the prior nested `group` payload in addition to the new top-level representation, or version/document the endpoint and provide a migration path before removing nested-payload support.
raw_findings.title: Preserve the existing nested create payload contract
raw_findings.trigger: An existing admin API client posts the previously supported payload shape, such as `{ group: { name: "team", visible: "true" } }`.

raw_findings.body: The request now falls through to the ordinary update path, returns success, and applies none of the requested membership changes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legacy membership updates become silent no-ops.
raw_findings.impact: The request now falls through to the ordinary update path, returns success, and applies none of the requested membership changes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The request-method dispatch to the incremental membership update implementation was removed while the resource route still accepts PATCH.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a PATCH branch that translates the legacy `changes` payload to add/remove operations, or return a clear versioned deprecation error rather than silently succeeding.
raw_findings.title: Retain PATCH membership-update handling or reject it explicitly
raw_findings.trigger: An existing client sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with the formerly supported `changes[add]` or `changes[delete]` membership payload.

raw_findings.body: Because PATCH now executes this unconditional assignment, the group is saved with `visible` set to false in addition to ignoring the requested membership update.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A membership-management request unexpectedly changes group visibility.
raw_findings.impact: Because PATCH now executes this unconditional assignment, the group is saved with `visible` set to false in addition to ignoring the requested membership update.
raw_findings.root_cause: The consolidated update action treats a partial membership PATCH as a full top-level representation and coerces an absent visibility field to false.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the separate PATCH membership path, and only assign `visible` when that field is supplied for a full group update.
raw_findings.title: Do not reset visibility on legacy PATCH membership requests
raw_findings.trigger: A client issues a formerly supported PATCH membership request containing only `changes` and no top-level `visible` parameter.
